title: Write a minimal complete artifact first, then refine in place (checkpoint-first)
statement: Under any hard wall-clock cap, have each step emit a schema-valid minimal complete output within the first seconds and then improve it in place, so a kill degrades quality instead of destroying the step.
rationale: Runtimes often impose a per-step timeout the author did not set. If work is written only at the end, a kill loses everything; if a minimal artifact exists early, the same kill costs only the refinement.
applies_when: Steps run under a per-step or per-stage timeout
Losing a step's work is expensive
not_when: Trivially short steps that always finish well under the cap
how: Have the step write a minimal valid output immediately
Refine that same file in place for the rest of the budget
Report the per-step duration DISTRIBUTION so a chronically over-budget step is visible
check: If a step is killed at a random time, does a valid (if rough) output already exist on disk? If not, it is not checkpoint-first.
failure_if_absent: A step that was still composing its answer when the timeout fired scores as producing nothing, and hours of correct work are lost.

evidence.title: agent-failure-modes INC-0002 - the hard per-step wall-clock cap
evidence.quote: A per-step timeout you did not set is often the real timeout. If a step's attempt logs are all the same tiny size, its median is AT the cap, not near it. Fix: write-early checkpoint
